reference: 1983, D.S. Evans, A. Prince, Mater. Res. Soc. Symp. Proc. 19 (1983) 383.
comment: DERIVED phase constraints (not measured): invariant-temperature brackets from the printed invariant reactions of invariants/AU-PB/AuPb-04Wan-LB.zpf-04.json (ORCHID literature values, Version 1, machine-extracted). Rule: README.md, 'Phase constraints'. Source ORCHID observation ids: ORC-F7PW5TESGT

orchid.rule: For each binary invariant reaction (eutectic, peritectic, monotectic, eutectoid, peritectoid, metatectic, syntectic, congruent melting or transformation, polymorphic) with printed temperature T and printed temperature uncertainty u (else u = 5 K, documented default), two ZPF points are written at the invariant composition x0: at T + max(2u, 10 K) the phase set stable above the reaction and at T - max(2u, 10 K) the set stable below. The reaction is read as printed with the cooling convention (left side = high temperature; a reaction written on heating, i.e. a single liquid formed from solids, is turned round). x0 is the composition of the phase alone on its side (eutectic: the liquid; peritectic: the product; congruent: the common composition); the other side's phases are written with their printed compositions (null where not printed or for line compounds, E2). The target hyperplane is estimated at x0 - d and x0 + d (d = min(0.01, half the distance to the nearest printed composition or to a pure element)) so that a line compound at x0 cannot make the hyperplane undefined (ESPEI 0.9.1 returns zero driving force when the equilibrium at the hyperplane composition is a single phase without internal degrees of freedom). A point is not written when another invariant of the system that shares a non-liquid phase (or a liquid within 0.05 in composition of x0) lies between T and the bracket temperature. These points encode the semantics of the printed reaction (which phases are stable on which side); they are DERIVED, not measured.
